items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Max Gordon couldn’t stand it. He told me in the ’80s, when we were with Quest.

ctx.x: I only remember her name. That’s all. We were opposite her. We played those four nights, and Pete, who had been gunning for this gig, bothering Max [Gordon]. “We going to be playing the Vanguard. We’re going to be playing the Vanguard.” Max finally gave him a gig. Then, the night after, he says, “I’m finished.” He says, “That’s it. They don’t want me back. I’m not playing anymore. I’m going to become a lawyer.” I said, “What?” And sure enough, the year later I saw the guy at NYU. He had books up to the ceiling.
As I heard it, he was driving a cab for a living.
